THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Accused No.1 in Crime No.186/2023 registered by the Kadur Police Station, Chikkamagaluru District, for the offences punishable under Sections 306, 324, 498A and 504 r/w Section 34 of IPC.,
is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. On the basis of the complaint dated 17.7.2023 lodged by Gaviranga s/o late Veeraswamy, FIR was registered in Crime No.186/2023 by the Kadur Police Station, Chikkamagaluru District, against the petitioner and four others initially for the offences punishable under NC: 2023:KHC:46109 Sections 302, 498A r/w 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, but later charge sheet was filed for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306, 324, 504 and 34 of IPC.
4.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner was arrested on 18.7.2023.
The investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
The petitioner has been arraigned as accused No.1 in the charge sheet.
His bail application filed before the Court of I Additional Sessions and Special Judge, Chikkamagaluru, in Criminal Misc. No.789/2023 has been dismissed on 15.11.2023.

7. FIR in Crime No.186/2023 was registered by the Kadur Police Station, Chikkamagaluru District initially for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 498A r/w 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act on the basis of the complaint lodged by Gaviranga s/o Veeraswamy, who is the father of the deceased Rukmini, wife of the petitioner herein.
The petitioner was arrested during the course of investigation on 18.7.2023.
The investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
The postmortem report of the deceased Rukmini would go to show that 'the death was due to Asphyxia as a result of hanging'.
Therefore, it is clear that the death was not homicidal.

Therefore, charge sheet is filed for the offence under Section 306 IPC.
NC: 2023:KHC:46109 8.
The marriage of the petitioner with the deceased Rukmini had taken place about 13 years prior to the date of the complaint and from the wedlock, the petitioner has two children.
As per the complaint and charge sheet allegations, the deceased was ill-treated in her matrimonial house by the accused persons.
This was allegedly informed by the deceased to her parents.
On 9.7.2023, the petitioner allegedly had assaulted deceased Rukmini on the ground that she had returned to her matrimonial house belatedly from her parental house.

The deceased had committed suicide by hanging herself on 16.7.2023 and the complaint was lodged by her father on 17.7.2023.
9.

On reading of the complaint as well as the charge sheet allegation, it is found that there is no allegation that on 16.7.2023 or immediately prior to the said date, the petitioner and other accused had abused or ill-treated the deceased which would have instigated or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
Undisputedly, the petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
He is in custody since 18.7.2023.
The investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
The apprehension of the learned HCGP that he may tamper with the prosecution witnesses can be taken care of by imposing stringent conditions.
11. Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of regular bail.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
